verified_facts: OS Open UPRN includes records independently of lifecycle state
under-construction, in-use and demolished UPRNs are included
an addressable location can be a building, commercial object or a non-standard object such as a pond or bus shelter
lifecycle inclusion means current-use status cannot be inferred from dataset presence alone
UPRN is supplied as an integer attribute with size 12
X and Y coordinates are British National Grid values with two decimal places
latitude and longitude are ETRS89 values with seven decimal places
GeoPackage geometry is a point representing the address-record location
NSUL and ONSUD cover Great Britain and are released every six weeks
ONSUD allocates address records to administrative and other geographies using the UPRN grid reference
ONSUD uses point-in-polygon for higher-geography allocation
ONSUD output is not parcel-boundary evidence
fixed availability is a January 2026 snapshot
fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access availability are reported
headline gigabit and full-fibre coverage focuses on residential properties
full-fibre take-up and premises without decent broadband use residential and commercial premises combined
fixed coverage downloads describe maximum available services
fixed performance describes active customer connections
postcode fixed-performance files are not published under the methodology used since July 2024
postcode coverage cannot be converted into measured connection performance
OS Open Linked Identifiers publishes authoritative relationships between UPRNs, USRNs and TOIDs
TopographicArea TOIDs can represent either a building outline or a road-surface area
feature role must be known before a TopographicArea relationship can support a property candidate
a road-surface TopographicArea must not be promoted as a property or parcel polygon
